name: Phoenix and Science
description: Phoenix has decided to become a scientist! He is currently investigating the growth of bacteria. Initially, on day $$$1$$$, there is one bacterium with mass $$$1$$$. Every day, some number of bacteria will split (possibly zero or all). When a bacterium of mass $$$m$$$ splits, it becomes two bacteria of mass $$$\frac{m}{2}$$$ each. For example, a bacterium of mass $$$3$$$ can split into two bacteria of mass $$$1.5$$$. Also, every night, the mass of every bacteria will increase by one. Phoenix is wondering if it is possible for the total mass of all the bacteria to be exactly $$$n$$$. If it is possible, he is interested in the way to obtain that mass using the minimum possible number of nights. Help him become the best scientist!
input_specification: The input consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^9$$$) — the sum of bacteria masses that Phoenix is interested in.
output_specification: For each test case, if there is no way for the bacteria to exactly achieve total mass $$$n$$$, print -1 . Otherwise, print two lines. The first line should contain an integer $$$d$$$  — the minimum number of nights needed. The next line should contain $$$d$$$ integers, with the $$$i$$$-th integer representing the number of bacteria that should split on the $$$i$$$-th day. If there are multiple solutions, print any.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1348D — Phoenix and Science [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
